AdminInsights.description: §7 Insights: reporting over data the platform already keeps; no new tracking.
AdminInsights.title: AdminInsights

AdminOrgDeletionUpdate.description: Give a pending deletion request a different grace period, counted from now.
AdminOrgDeletionUpdate.title: AdminOrgDeletionUpdate

AdminOrgPlanChange.description: A manual plan change, for orgs not billed through Stripe. Needs a reason (§6.5).
AdminOrgPlanChange.title: AdminOrgPlanChange

AdminOrgRead.description: Operator-facing view of an organization: metadata, counts, plan, status.
AdminOrgRead.title: AdminOrgRead

AdminOrgSeatOverride.description: Operator sets a per-org seat override above the plan cap, with a reason.
AdminOrgSeatOverride.title: AdminOrgSeatOverride

AdminProjectRead.description: Metadata only. Administrators run the platform; they do not get to read customer specs.
AdminProjectRead.title: AdminProjectRead

AuthConfigRead.description: Response body for auth config endpoints.
AuthConfigRead.title: AuthConfigRead

AuthConfigUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /projects/{id}/auth.

All fields optional — only supplied fields are updated.
Cross-field rules are re-checked after merging current state with the patch.
AuthConfigUpdate.title: AuthConfigUpdate

AuthCustomFieldRead.description: Response body for auth custom field endpoints.
AuthCustomFieldRead.title: AuthCustomFieldRead

AuthCustomFieldType.description: Field types available for custom registration fields on generated projects.
AuthCustomFieldType.title: AuthCustomFieldType

AuthOperation.description:
Entity operations that can have RBAC permissions attached.

`replace` shadows `str.replace`; the type: ignore is required because mypy's
str-inheritance check flags it as an incompatible assignment even though
the enum semantics are correct.
AuthOperation.title: AuthOperation

AuthProvider.description: Where a generated project's users and tokens come from.
AuthProvider.title: AuthProvider

AuthSecretsStatus.description:
Response body for GET /projects/{id}/auth/secrets/status and PUT.

Returns booleans only — never plaintext or ciphertext credentials.
AuthSecretsStatus.title: AuthSecretsStatus

AuthSecretsWrite.description:
Request body for PUT /projects/{id}/auth/secrets.

Send only the credential groups that changed.  Omitting a group leaves
any previously stored secrets for that group intact (partial update).
Sending a group with null/missing fields clears that group.

Cross-validation: if sms_provider is specified, the matching secret
block must be present.
AuthSecretsWrite.title: AuthSecretsWrite

AuthorizationModel.description:
How a generated project decides who may do what.

rbac  roles and per-operation permissions with row rules (the original model)
abac  attribute-based: policies over subject, resource and environment attributes, all
      applying to every signed-in person (NIST SP 800-162)
pbac  policy-based: named policies attached to roles; allow and deny effects. PBAC has no
      standard definition: this is the meaning used here, and the docs say so
AuthorizationModel.title: AuthorizationModel

AuthorizationWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/authorization (replaces the whole block).
AuthorizationWrite.title: AuthorizationWrite

DeletionMode.description: How user records are removed in generated projects.
DeletionMode.title: DeletionMode

DeploymentPlan.description: What the settings turn into: concrete numbers and the tfvars files, for a live preview.
DeploymentPlan.title: DeploymentPlan

DeploymentWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/deployment. `expected_version` guards against lost updates.
DeploymentWrite.title: DeploymentWrite

DismissBody.description:
Body of POST /projects/{id}/status/dismiss. `step` must be a dismissable step id
(today: `consider_auth`); anything else is a 422.
DismissBody.title: DismissBody

DocumentsWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/documents. `expected_version` guards against lost updates.
DocumentsWrite.title: DocumentsWrite

DownloadMode.description: proxy: the API streams the file. presigned: the API redirects to a short-lived signed URL.
DownloadMode.title: DownloadMode

HistoryWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/history. Replaces every change-history config.
HistoryWrite.title: HistoryWrite

HooksWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/hooks. Replaces every hook declaration.
HooksWrite.title: HooksWrite

IdentityProvider.description:
One external login. The client secret is never stored: it is an environment variable
(KC_IDP_<ALIAS>_CLIENT_SECRET) of the generated project.
IdentityProvider.title: IdentityProvider

IdpType.description: Kinds of external login a Keycloak realm can offer.
IdpType.title: IdpType

ImpersonationDigestRead.description: Preview of the daily support-access digest (nothing is sent).
ImpersonationDigestRead.title: ImpersonationDigestRead

ImpersonationRequest.description: Why the operator needs to see what the member sees. Kept in the audit trail.
ImpersonationRequest.title: ImpersonationRequest

ImpersonationStarted.description: The only response that ever carries the "view as" access token.
ImpersonationStarted.title: ImpersonationStarted

ImpersonationState.description: What the "You are viewing as X" banner shows.
ImpersonationState.title: ImpersonationState

JwtAlgorithm.description: Signing algorithm for access tokens in generated projects.
JwtAlgorithm.title: JwtAlgorithm

KeycloakConfigWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/keycloak. Omitted ids default from the project slug.
KeycloakConfigWrite.title: KeycloakConfigWrite

KeycloakImpact.description: What switching would change, shown before the user confirms.
KeycloakImpact.title: KeycloakImpact

KeycloakMode.description: own: the project ships its own Keycloak. shared: it trusts an existing realm.
KeycloakMode.title: KeycloakMode

KeycloakSwitchRequest.description:
Body of POST .../keycloak/enable and .../keycloak/disable: switching the identity
provider is deliberate, so the caller must say so.
KeycloakSwitchRequest.title: KeycloakSwitchRequest

ListsWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/lists. Replaces every list.
ListsWrite.title: ListsWrite

LoginDiscoverRead.description: `sso`: send the browser to `login_url`. `password`: show the password form.
LoginDiscoverRead.title: LoginDiscoverRead

MemberRole.description: A person's role inside one project. Ordered: viewer < editor < owner.
MemberRole.title: MemberRole

MfaChallengeRead.description:
The answer to a correct password when a second step is needed. No session yet.

`enrollment_required`: the account must set up TOTP first (platform staff without it): call
`…/login/mfa/setup` then `…/login/mfa/enable`. Otherwise send a code to `…/login/mfa`.
MfaChallengeRead.title: MfaChallengeRead

ObservabilityWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/observability. `expected_version` guards against lost updates.
ObservabilityWrite.title: ObservabilityWrite

OrgAuditRead.description:
An org admin's view of the audit log (§8). No `detail` and no client IP: §7.1 keeps
request details that can contain customer data out of shared views.
OrgAuditRead.title: OrgAuditRead

OrgKind.description: Shape of an organization: a one-member account versus a multi-member team.
OrgKind.title: OrgKind

OrgPoliciesRead.description:
§8 Security policies. `session_ttl_hours` None = the platform default
(`default_session_hours`).
OrgPoliciesRead.title: OrgPoliciesRead

OrgPoliciesUpdate.description: Only the fields sent change. `session_ttl_hours: null` goes back to the default.
OrgPoliciesUpdate.title: OrgPoliciesUpdate

OrgRole.description: A person's role inside one organization. Ordered: member < admin < owner.
OrgRole.title: OrgRole

PaymentProvider.description: Payment service providers the generated payments module can talk to.
PaymentProvider.title: PaymentProvider

PaymentsAvailability.description: single: one of everything is acceptable. ha: no single process may be a point of failure.
PaymentsAvailability.title: PaymentsAvailability

PaymentsProfile.description: Starting point for the sizing numbers; any number the user sets wins.
PaymentsProfile.title: PaymentsProfile

PaymentsSizingRead.description: Derived deployment shape for the saved scale settings (no side effects).
PaymentsSizingRead.title: PaymentsSizingRead

PaymentsSwitchRequest.description:
Body of POST .../payments/enable and .../payments/disable: both change what the next
generated project contains, so the caller must say so.
PaymentsSwitchRequest.title: PaymentsSwitchRequest

PermissionEntry.description: A single (entity × operation) permission slot in a bulk upsert.
PermissionEntry.title: PermissionEntry

PlanWrite.description: Operator-facing plan editor. The id is immutable once created.
PlanWrite.title: PlanWrite

PlatformRole.description: What a person may do on the platform itself, independent of any project.
PlatformRole.title: PlatformRole

PreviewRequest.description: Render a template with data and return the PDF, without saving anything.
PreviewRequest.title: PreviewRequest

ProjectPermissionBulkUpsert.description:
Request body for POST /projects/{id}/permissions (full matrix replace).

Entries with duplicate (entity_id, operation) pairs within the same request
are rejected by the service before touching the DB.
ProjectPermissionBulkUpsert.title: ProjectPermissionBulkUpsert

ProjectTokenRead.description: An API token as seen by a project owner — includes whose token it is.
ProjectTokenRead.title: ProjectTokenRead

RecommendRequest.description: Answers to the wizard. Every field has a neutral default so a partial form still works.
RecommendRequest.title: RecommendRequest

RecoveryCodesRead.description: Shown once. Each code works one time instead of an authenticator code.
RecoveryCodesRead.title: RecoveryCodesRead

RenameHint.description: A declared rename. Entity rename: `{from, to}`. Field rename: `{entity, from, to}`.
RenameHint.title: RenameHint

RolesRead.description:
GET /projects/{id}/behavior/roles: the role names declared by the project's auth config, for
the role pickers of the behaviour pages. Empty when sign-in has no roles (or is not set up).
Readable by anyone who can read the project spec; carries names and labels only.
RolesRead.title: RolesRead

RowRule.description: Row-level access rule applied by the generator to entity CRUD queries.
RowRule.title: RowRule

ScimTokenRead.description: POST /orgs/{slug}/scim/token. `token` is shown this once; only its hash is kept.
ScimTokenRead.title: ScimTokenRead

SeedGeneratorBody.description:
One generator of a seed plan. Shapes and sizes only; which keys a type takes and whether the values
fit the column is `validation.validate`'s job.
SeedGeneratorBody.title: SeedGeneratorBody

SeedWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/seed. Replaces every seed profile.
SeedWrite.title: SeedWrite

SequencesWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/sequences. Replaces every sequence.
SequencesWrite.title: SequencesWrite

SessionRead.description: Access token in the body (the app keeps it in memory); the refresh token is a cookie.
SessionRead.title: SessionRead

SessionWithRecoveryCodesRead.description: TOTP was just turned on: a fresh session that counts as MFA'd, plus the backup codes.
SessionWithRecoveryCodesRead.title: SessionWithRecoveryCodesRead

SettingsWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/settings. Replaces every setting.
SettingsWrite.title: SettingsWrite

SmsConfig.description:
Non-secret SMS provider settings.

from_number follows E.164 format (+<country><number>).
Actual API credentials (auth_token, API key) must live in env vars.
SmsConfig.title: SmsConfig

SmsProvider.description: Third-party SMS gateway for OTP delivery.
SmsProvider.title: SmsProvider

SmtpConfig.description:
SMTP server settings embedded in auth config.

Credentials (password) are never stored here; they live in env vars of
the generated project.
SmtpConfig.title: SmtpConfig

SmtpSecretsWrite.description:
SMTP credential fragment.

`username` is optional — many providers (SendGrid, Mailgun) use a fixed
username ("apikey", "api") and only need the API key as password.
SmtpSecretsWrite.title: SmtpSecretsWrite

SpecApiEdge.description:
The API edge (C14), off unless `enabled`: idempotency keys, rate limits and quotas, dated API
versions. Each part is on when its section is present.
SpecApiEdge.title: SpecApiEdge

SpecApiVersioning.description:
Dated API versions. `default` is what a client without an `API-Version` header gets; the newest
version's shape is the one the code produces, older ones come from transformers in
app/hooks/api_versions.py.
SpecApiVersioning.title: SpecApiVersioning

SpecAuthSecrets.description:
Decrypted credentials injected at generation time.

This model is NEVER serialised in HTTP responses.  It is populated
by the generation service after calling AuthSecretsService.get_for_generator()
and exists solely so Jinja templates can reference credentials by name.
SpecAuthSecrets.title: SpecAuthSecrets

SpecDeployEnvironment.description: One environment (dev, staging, prod ...). `profile` fills every number left empty.
SpecDeployEnvironment.title: SpecDeployEnvironment

SpecDeployment.description:
CI/CD workflows and Terraform for one cloud. No cloud credential is ever stored: pipelines
sign in with short-lived OIDC tokens (one-time trust setup: deploy/<cloud>/bootstrap).
SpecDeployment.title: SpecDeployment

SpecDocTemplate.description: One PDF template: the plain-data structure `doc_engine` renders, plus who may render it.
SpecDocTemplate.title: SpecDocTemplate

SpecDocuments.description: PDF documents (invoice, receipt, statement ...) rendered by the generated API.
SpecDocuments.title: SpecDocuments

SpecEvents.description:
Transactional outbox and typed event bus (C10). Off unless `enabled`. Every entity gets
created / updated / deleted events, and every state machine a `<entity>.transitioned` event; each
is written to the outbox in the write's own transaction and delivered at least once, in order per
record, by a relay. `adapter` is where events go: `in_process` (subscribers in the same app) or
`redis_streams` (not implemented yet). Delivered rows are purged after `retention_days`.
SpecEvents.title: SpecEvents

SpecHistory.description:
Change history for one entity: every create, update and delete of the listed `fields` is
recorded with the actor, the old value and the new value, and kept for `retention_days`.
Only the listed fields are ever recorded. `view_roles` may read an entity's history through the
API; empty = nobody (fail closed).
SpecHistory.title: SpecHistory

SpecHook.description:
A piece of custom logic under contract. The spec declares the name, where it runs (`point`),
what goes in and what must come out; the platform generates the models, the stub file, the wiring
and the gates. The body is free Python inside the marked region of the stub.

point: `<Entity>.before_save | validate | after_save | after_commit` or
`<Entity>.transition_guard(<manual transition>)`. kind: `pure` (no I/O) or `effect` (only at
after_commit). failure_policy empty = the default for the point (guards and validate: fail_closed,
effects: fail_open, other pure hooks: fail_closed). `fallback` gives the output values used by the
`fallback` policy. `reads` lists the entities an effect hook may read through the SDK.
SpecHook.title: SpecHook

SpecHookBudget.description: Resource limits of one call: wall-clock milliseconds, rows read through the SDK, outbound calls.
SpecHookBudget.title: SpecHookBudget

SpecHookEffectBudget.description:
Limits of an effectful hook (H3): outbound calls per effect type in one invocation, the largest
payload of one call in bytes, and outbound calls per minute for the hook (per API process).
The wall-clock limit is `budget.cpu_ms`. Breaking any limit aborts the hook (its failure policy applies).
SpecHookEffectBudget.title: SpecHookEffectBudget

SpecHookEffects.description:
Per-project opt-in for effectful hooks (H2). OFF unless `enabled`. Hooks are written by TRUSTED
authors only until the Cycle 3 sandbox exists: `trusted_authors_only` must be true to turn this on.
`webhook_hosts` is the allow-list of hosts a hook may post to (SSRF guard still applies).
SpecHookEffects.title: SpecHookEffects

SpecHookField.description:
One scalar field of a hook's input or output model. The platform generates the Pydantic model
from the list. `type` is string | int | float | decimal | bool | date | datetime | uuid.
SpecHookField.title: SpecHookField

SpecIdempotency.description: `Idempotency-Key` on the listed methods: the same key and request replays the first response.
SpecIdempotency.title: SpecIdempotency

SpecIdentityProvider.description:
One external login offered by the Keycloak realm. The client secret is never part of
the spec: the generated project reads it from KC_IDP_<ALIAS>_CLIENT_SECRET.
SpecIdentityProvider.title: SpecIdentityProvider

SpecJob.description:
A kind of background job. `handler` is the name of a function you write in the custom file
app/hooks/jobs.py (the platform generates only the registry and the stub).
SpecJob.title: SpecJob

SpecJobQueue.description:
Where jobs wait. Only `postgres` (the app's own database, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) is
implemented; `redis` and `rabbitmq` are accepted by the schema and refused by validation.
SpecJobQueue.title: SpecJobQueue

SpecJobRetry.description:
How a failing job is tried again: up to `max_attempts` runs in all, waiting `backoff_seconds`
(`fixed`) or `backoff_seconds` doubling each time (`exponential`, capped at an hour) between runs.
After the last failed run the job is parked as `dead` (visible, and it can be requeued).
SpecJobRetry.title: SpecJobRetry

SpecJobSchedule.description:
Enqueue `job` on a 5-field `cron` in `timezone`. Exactly one job per tick, however many worker
processes run. If ticks were missed (everything was down), `missed` decides: `catch_up_one` runs
the most recent missed tick once, `skip` drops them.
SpecJobSchedule.title: SpecJobSchedule

SpecJobs.description: Background jobs, schedules and worker groups (C11). Off unless `enabled`.
SpecJobs.title: SpecJobs

SpecList.description:
A named list of values (statuses, categories ...). `items` is the system default set; a
tenant (or the whole project when single-tenant) may add values, relabel, recolour, reorder and
switch off the unlocked ones, if it holds one of `edit_roles`.
SpecList.title: SpecList

SpecNotificationTemplate.description:
The default template of one notification type for one channel. `{{ name }}` placeholders may
only name the type's declared `variables` (no expressions, no filters). For email, `html: true`
makes the body HTML: every variable is HTML-escaped. `subject` is the email subject / push title.
SpecNotificationTemplate.title: SpecNotificationTemplate

SpecNotificationType.description:
One kind of notification. `category`: `transactional` (always sent) or `optional` (a user can opt
out per channel). `on_event` (e.g. `order.created`) sends it when that event is delivered by the
outbox: `recipient_key_field` is the event-data field naming the recipient (a user id, compared with
the preferences) and `address_fields` maps each channel to the data field holding the address.
SpecNotificationType.title: SpecNotificationType

SpecNotifications.description:
Notifications over the provider adapters (C17). Off unless `enabled`. Needs `providers` and auth.
Messages are queued as delivery-log rows and sent by a dispatcher with retries and backoff.
SpecNotifications.title: SpecNotifications

SpecObservability.description:
OpenTelemetry in the generated service: traces and metrics over OTLP/HTTP, log correlation.

Everything an operator tunes in production (endpoint, sampler, service name) stays an
environment variable of the generated project; this block only sets the defaults and what is
generated. No endpoint or header (they may hold credentials) is ever stored here.
SpecObservability.title: SpecObservability

SpecOpApply.description:
`op_type` must be one of the registry's operations; `payload` is checked against that
operation's own model.
SpecOpApply.title: SpecOpApply

SpecPayments.description:
Card payments through a hosted checkout. Provider secrets are never part of the spec:
the generated project reads them from its environment.
SpecPayments.title: SpecPayments

SpecPaymentsPayable.description: The entity a payment is for (e.g. Order): where the amount, currency and status live.
SpecPaymentsPayable.title: SpecPaymentsPayable

SpecPaymentsRoles.description: Who may do what. An empty list means nobody (fail closed), unlike entity permissions.
SpecPaymentsRoles.title: SpecPaymentsRoles

SpecPaymentsScale.description:
Expected load. `payments_sizing.size()` turns it into replicas, pools and worker counts;
any explicit override below wins over the computed number.
SpecPaymentsScale.title: SpecPaymentsScale

SpecPaymentsSecurity.description: Security knobs. Every one has a floor or ceiling that validation enforces.
SpecPaymentsSecurity.title: SpecPaymentsSecurity

SpecPolicy.description: One authorization policy (abac / pbac). `when` is plain data, never code: see authz_engine.
SpecPolicy.title: SpecPolicy

SpecProviderAdapter.description:
One adapter a project may use: its `kind` (email | sms | push | payments | storage | llm |
generic), its `name` and NON-SECRET settings. Credentials are never part of the spec: each tenant
writes its own through the generated, admin-only vault API.
SpecProviderAdapter.title: SpecProviderAdapter

SpecProviders.description:
Provider adapter framework and per-tenant credential vault (C15). Off unless `enabled`.
Every kind always has the in-process `emulator`; the adapters listed here are the ones a tenant
may select by storing credentials for them. Nothing secret lives in the spec (`secret_in_spec`).
SpecProviders.title: SpecProviders

SpecQuota.description:
A hard cap on a named meter per tenant and period (`day` or `month`, UTC). Requests whose method
is in `methods` (empty = all) and whose path is under `path_prefix` use `cost` of the meter.
SpecQuota.title: SpecQuota

SpecRateBucket.description: A token bucket: holds at most `capacity` tokens and gets `refill_per_second` back each second.
SpecRateBucket.title: SpecRateBucket

SpecRateGroup.description:
Limits for a group of routes (first matching group wins; `methods` empty = every method).
`user` / `tenant` replace the defaults for this group (callers without a valid token always use
`anonymous`); `cost` is what one request takes out.
SpecRateGroup.title: SpecRateGroup

SpecRateLimits.description:
Rate limits per (tenant, caller) and per tenant, stored in Postgres so they hold across processes.
Callers without a valid token are limited per client address (`anonymous`). A store error refuses
writes with 503; reads are refused too unless `read_fail_open`.
SpecRateLimits.title: SpecRateLimits

SpecSeedEntity.description: `count` rows of `entity` (for each tenant when the entity is tenant-scoped).
SpecSeedEntity.title: SpecSeedEntity

SpecSeedGenerator.description:
How one column of a seeded row gets its value. `type` is one of a CLOSED set (see
validation_seed.GENERATORS); each type accepts only its own keys, anything else is refused.
The plan holds data only: no code, no SQL, no expressions.
SpecSeedGenerator.title: SpecSeedGenerator

SpecSeedProfile.description:
One named, reproducible data set (demo, dev ...). The same profile always yields the same rows:
`seed` drives every random choice and `as_of` is the only clock (no wall-clock time is read).
`tenants` is the number of tenants to create and must be 0 unless the project is multi-tenant.
SpecSeedProfile.title: SpecSeedProfile

SpecSequence.description:
A gapless counter: a number is consumed only when the caller's transaction commits.
Numbers look like `<prefix>[<year>-]<zero padded counter>`.
SpecSequence.title: SpecSequence

SpecSetting.description:
A typed value the running service reads and a role may change at run time (per tenant when
the project is multi-tenant). `default` is what everybody gets until a value is saved.
Settings are for business knobs, never secrets: names that look like credentials are refused.
SpecSetting.title: SpecSetting

SpecStateMachine.description:
A lifecycle for one entity. The states are the `enum_values` of `field`, which must be a
required enum field; callers cannot write it directly, only move it through transitions.
SpecStateMachine.title: SpecStateMachine

SpecStorage.description:
File uploads into an S3-compatible bucket, scanned for malware before they are stored.
Bucket credentials are never part of the spec: the generated project reads them from its
environment.
SpecStorage.title: SpecStorage

SpecStorageRoles.description: Who may do what with files. An empty list means nobody (fail closed).
SpecStorageRoles.title: SpecStorageRoles

SpecStorageSecurity.description: Security knobs. Every one has a floor or ceiling that validation enforces.
SpecStorageSecurity.title: SpecStorageSecurity

SpecSuiteRef.description:
Reserved: this app is one of several that share a sign-in hub. Empty (None on SpecAuth)
for every project that has not opted in; the generator ignores it for now.
SpecSuiteRef.title: SpecSuiteRef

SpecTransition.description:
One allowed move of a state machine: from any of `from_states` to `to_state`.

`when` is an expression (app/core/expr) over the record's own fields: the move is refused
unless it is true (null counts as false). `roles` limits who may trigger it. With NO roles
the move is open to anyone who may UPDATE the entity (default deny): the caller must pass the same
update access as PATCH / PUT (roles, row rules or policies), so a read-only role cannot move a
record. To let a role move records without edit rights, list that role here. `auto` moves are applied by the platform right after a write
whenever their guard holds, so they never have `roles`.
SpecTransition.title: SpecTransition

SpecWebhookInbound.description:
One incoming webhook receiver, served at POST /webhooks/in/<name>. Requests must carry a valid
Standard Webhooks signature (raw body, HMAC-SHA256) made with a secret the admin stored for this
endpoint; the handler is a function you write in app/hooks/webhooks.py.
SpecWebhookInbound.title: SpecWebhookInbound

SpecWebhooks.description:
Webhooks out and in (C13). Off unless `enabled`. Needs events (the source of outgoing webhooks),
jobs (retries with backoff: declare a job `webhook_delivery`) and providers (the vault that keeps
the signing secrets). Nothing secret lives in the spec. Only `events` listed here can be subscribed
to (default deny); URLs must pass the SSRF guard (public addresses only, no redirects followed).
SpecWebhooks.title: SpecWebhooks

SpecWorkerGroup.description:
A set of worker processes that run jobs from the listed `queues`, `concurrency` jobs at a time
per process. `same_server` adds a compose service to the project; `separate_server` writes a
bundle under deploy/workers/<name>/ to run on another machine with its own DATABASE_URL.
SpecWorkerGroup.title: SpecWorkerGroup

SpecWorkflow.description:
A durable saga: ordered `steps` run one at a time and each completed step is recorded in Postgres,
so a crashed or restarted worker resumes after the last completed step. `on_failure`: `compensate`
undoes completed steps in reverse order, `fail` stops and leaves them. `roles` may start, inspect and
cancel runs (default deny: at least one is required).
SpecWorkflow.title: SpecWorkflow

SpecWorkflowRetry.description: How a failing workflow step is tried again before the workflow counts it as failed.
SpecWorkflowRetry.title: SpecWorkflowRetry

SpecWorkflowStep.description:
One step. `kind: hook` runs the function you write in app/hooks/workflows.py for (workflow, step);
`kind: job` enqueues the declared background job `job` (atomically with recording the step) and counts
as done once enqueued. `compensate` says the step has an undo function (run in reverse order when a
later step fails or the run is cancelled); set it false only for a step that needs no undo.
SpecWorkflowStep.title: SpecWorkflowStep

SpecWorkflowWorker.description: The worker process that executes runs (`python -m app.workflows.worker`).
SpecWorkflowWorker.title: SpecWorkflowWorker

SpecWorkflows.description:
Durable workflows (C12), off unless `enabled`. `runtime`: `postgres` is the built-in durable
runner; `dbos` and `temporal` are accepted by the schema and refused by validation (not_yet_implemented).
SpecWorkflows.title: SpecWorkflows

SsoConfigUpdate.description:
PUT /orgs/{slug}/sso. Fields of the other protocol are ignored and cleared.

`oidc_client_secret` may be omitted on later saves to keep the stored one.
SsoConfigUpdate.title: SsoConfigUpdate

SsoServiceProviderRead.description: What the org admin pastes into their IdP.
SsoServiceProviderRead.title: SsoServiceProviderRead

SsoTestRead.description: The last "test with my own e-mail" round trip (§12.D.6).
SsoTestRead.title: SsoTestRead

SsoTestStart.description:
Open `login_url` in the browser (a full navigation, not fetch): it goes to the IdP and
comes back to `#/org/<slug>/sso?sso_test=<result>` without signing anyone in.
SsoTestStart.title: SsoTestStart

StateMachinesWrite.description: Body of PUT /projects/{id}/behavior/state-machines. Replaces every machine.
StateMachinesWrite.title: StateMachinesWrite

StorageBackend.description: Where uploaded files live. Both speak the S3 API; minio is any self-hosted compatible server.
StorageBackend.title: StorageBackend

StorageIssues.description: Validation issues under `storage` (and file fields), without side effects.
StorageIssues.title: StorageIssues

StorageSwitchRequest.description:
Body of POST .../storage/enable and .../storage/disable: both change what the next
generated project contains, so the caller must say so.

A session, or `{mfa_required: true, mfa_token, …}` when a second step is needed
(TOTP on, or platform staff): then call `/account/login/mfa` (or the enrolment pair).

§4.2 step 1, tenant-first discovery: if the address's domain belongs to an org with
active SSO, the app sends the browser to `login_url`; otherwise it shows the password
form. Says nothing about whether an account exists, only about the domain.
Second step of a sign-in: a TOTP code or a recovery code for the challenge.
Enrolment challenge only: prove the first code, turn TOTP on and sign in.
Enrolment challenge only (staff without TOTP): a new secret to scan.
